question_text: What is the difference in the positions of a girl carrying a bag in one of her hands and another girl carrying a bag in each of her two hands?

verification.note: TSBIE Basic Learning Material (2021-22), Unit 7 VERY SHORT ANSWER — this question is NOT in the Sri Chaitanya Fastrack; the two source books are not supersets of each other, so the unit inventory is their union. The 1+1 split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Bag in one hand
lines: With a bag in ONE hand, the centre of
mass of the girl-and-bag system shifts
towards the hand holding the bag.
steps.margin_note: Name the system — girl AND bag together. The shift is of the combined centre of mass.
steps.why: Adding mass on one side moves the weighted average of all the mass towards that side. The girl leans the other way to bring it back over her feet.
common_mistakes: Saying the girl’s own centre of mass moves. It is the SYSTEM’s centre of mass that shifts.

recall.must_convey: That with one bag the centre of mass shifts towards the loaded hand.
accept: centre of mass shifts towards the bag
shifts to the side of the bag
bag unna side ki CM shift
reject: the centre of mass does not change

steps.label: Bags in both hands
lines: With equal bags in BOTH hands, the two

lines.text: the centre of mass does not change.

steps.margin_note: Give the reason — symmetry — not just the answer.
steps.why: Equal masses at equal distances on both sides pull the average equally both ways. This is why carrying two balanced bags feels straighter than one heavy one.
common_mistakes: Answering that the centre of mass "shifts down" — the question is about the sideways position.

recall.must_convey: That with a bag in each hand the shifts cancel and the centre of mass stays in place.
accept: centre of mass does not change
reject: centre of mass shifts towards the bag
